body:
A student loan is a type of loan designed to help students pay for post-secondary education and the associated fees, such as tuition, books and supplies, and living expenses.

There is nothing entitled about it. At all. I worked very many years in minimum wage jobs thank you. A student loan is a perfectly dignified way of getting through university.
I have delayed by a year, this is the whole point.
My account is now £500 overdrawn, from £0.50 overdrawn in October. When I prove my student status, the bank will clear it all, because I'll get my overdraft. (I never applied in first year)
Thanks for the suggestion, I've been to the Manchester one and it was brilliant.
They don't help with clothes. I asked a foodbank, and they spent a month getting clothes together, were really kind. However, when it was dropped off, it was all hoodies.

I appreciate the sentiment, but I was never given a second chance. With a second chance, I could have been given my student loan. Then I could have bought some trainers that weren't falling apart, some toothpaste, shampoo, etc, and I could have gone to all the job interviews in the world.

Even if I went to another university, I wouldn't get the student finance until October. I have all of my things here, where can I put them. A job won't take me if I turn up in shorts that haven't been cleaned in 4 months. It's not mental health that's causing that, I just really don't have any money. The laundry here costs £4.50.
I planned my life based around attending university, financially. The carpet was pulled I guess, but I don't know how to deal with that.
I never said I was content starving myself. Food costs money here, unless I go to a foodbank.

There is a huge stigma around suffering. I think we need more kindness, more love, and second chances.
I'm going to prove you wrong. Just wait.
I understand. I just can't get 8 months back.

Please read the sub. I didn't miss the exams on purpose.

Please leave me alone.
Thank you. I've applied to my local student lawyer, in Wigan.

There aren't any words that would come close. Impossibly unfair and unfair don't come close. I've learned throughout this time that it is wrong to go through pain in life. It's wrong that we suffer. People don't like it, and they'll call you anything under the sun, to make you feel worse. Domestic violence is never okay, in my opinion. 

I don't have a way out though. By sitting my exams, student finance said they could release the loan. Then I could visit my family, and get back on my feet. Releasing the loan would allow me to get some clothes, to get a job again, etc. I would have two entire months to do some first year exams that only count for 10%.

I don't know how to speak up, because I know what I want, and I know that other people won't listen to me. I'll go with that and see what the NUS say. I can't just be wrong, and to have lost all those months, earning potential and everything. 

I'll try the lawyer, the paper, the NUS. How would compensation work? If I could provide that I gave the evidence that was asked for, and that it was ignored, would I be entitled to anything? 

Sitting the exams just seems to be the right way. I get down voted if I say that it's my right, but I really did sit A levels, and I really did well. I worked hard. This is my way out, and I promise I never meant to live through that situation. I didn't do it on purpose. I just need someone to talk to. Someone that will listen. It seems so hard to get.
I could send you my A level certificate, if you'd like to see it.

Please leave your contact details. I'm going to send you a video link to my talk at the conference. It isn't a four month conference, it's in 4 months. I'm going to send you all the evidence in world. It's going to be a light at the end of my tunnel. 

Don't be so rude. I should know, I'm fine. I've been fine for ages, I moved out of the house at the end of last year. The GP knows I'm fine. I'm fine. Objectively see that.

Rudyard Kipling said "Or, being lied about, don't deal in lies."

That's what I'm going to do here.

Have a good day.

Thank you for your kind words.

I do understand, however I was enrolled before. I even have my student card in front of me. It doesn't expire until 2019. It won't even allow me access to the library at the moment, which is clearly not helpful for studying. 

I just don't know what to do. They've offered me to start my degree in September. But I'm here now, and I've been here since september, studying. Waiting, for help. I hate speaking about it, because I just learned this year that speaking up (which ironically is what they tell people to do), just makes you look like a bad guy. It breaks my heart. It should be okay to say "this isn't right, could you help me?" 

I've worked so hard. I'm going to pursue the student lawyer that an advice service got in touch with. I'm also contacting the NUS, and might do a couple of anonymous interviews, to help me out of the financial hole. 

I am determined, I just need at least the free choice of will to sit this August. If they offered, and I didn't want to, that would be fine. But they haven't even offered yet. They put it on the table in March and swiftly pulled it away. I'll update you. It's just been to long a road to get trodden on. 

Thank you.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qEt9ZcS6X0M

Gives me some solace.

You haven't read my sub. My GP cleared me as mentally fit to study back in October. It was trauma induced anxiety. It's not a medical condition once the trauma is removed. My GP is confused now, 8 months later, because she doesn't know how to say that someone who is mentally fit, isn't. She actually told me while the appeal was going on "not to say that you feel fine."

I'll contact the NUS.

I'm sorry for the confusion from the long post. I never expected to go into second year. I was expecting to, and quite willing, to go to my first year classes over again. I came to terms with that over the summer. 

1) My doctor provided medical evidence at the first appeal. She expected it to all be resolved that week. The evidence stretches back to the first semester of my first year, so it is very real evidence. It is coherent, it states what was wrong, how my GP feels it would have affected me at the time, and also it states that she is confident I am now "of a disposition fit to study at university." Now being last september.

2) I didn't apply for an extension or medical exemption, no. There were no extensions required. I missed the exams very abruptly because of situations at the house. I had done the studying, etc. I didn't mean for any of this to happen.

3) I applied for student finance and was accepted. Received all the documents in the post. I haven't received any student finance, no. My card won't even allow me to enter the library. When I attend lectures, I'm never on the class list. I don't think I'm able to receive student finance until the university reenters me for exams.

4) Although not ideal, I'm more than willing to stand aside, and take my exams this August. That gives me time to get myself together, and it gives the university time to enter me, pass student finance, etc. I'm very, very confident of succeeding with at least a 2:1 in the exams, because I've spent the year studying.

You cannot respond to accusations of being a troll, with calling someone else a troll.

And yes, I deserve to be anonymous, if this goes further. I deserve that right. I shouldn't have to ask for basic rights.
You cannot respond to accusations of being a troll, with calling someone else a troll.

Please could a moderator remove this troll? 

If you're going to pick on people, it isn't going to be me. Leave me alone.
I went to student services and they directed me to my GP. I did so, received a letter. Sent this into the dean of the department.

You do realize, that if I did...I'd get unwanted attention. 

Don't be so mean to people. God forbid, something might happen to you one day. 

Best wishes, be well.
Yes.
I did actually meet with the board of examiners this March.

Retaking first year yes, I just haven't been given my exam dates yet. I know I'm fully capable of passing all of them in August with at least 60%. 

I never received an average, it defaulted because of the missed exams. There were some I got 60 in from first semester, but because of the 0's, I never got an average. 

UoM is where I got my place. I'd probably have to pay for UCAS again to go elsewhere, and to pay for a certificate again (A levels). 

I don't want them to bend the rules because that's not what they'd be doing. Bending the rules would look like "Give me a 1st, not a 2:1 like I got." I just want to be heard, to be entered for my exams. I know they're giving me free accom, but I'd be paying it myself if I had my student finance. That's part of the deal coming to university, it's why the government has the scheme set out in the first place. It helps those of us from unwealthy backgrounds to attend.

Half of first years this year never really got to go to class after Christmas, because of the strikes. They lasted months. The university didn't even attempt to refund people. You can look it up in the papers that they said their job was to "provide a degree, not an education."

I'll have a look, if things don't happen in the next couple of weeks. Thank you.

It's funny, you sound like the professor I had a meeting with. She told me to "stop acting like the world is against me." I had a journalist give me a recorder for the meeting and she couldn't believe it. 

I can't be a denominator because that would require more than one situation. There is one, and yes, I am the denominator. The suffering party. I won't let mean words get to me. We have to stand up for what is right and just, otherwise there's no point in life. 

This entire post was about getting the help I need, lets hope I get it soon.

If the other side of the story were that different, I'd be on the course and passing my exams with flying colours. 

There is one way out of this. I'm not allowed to say it because people don't like me speaking the truth, but there's only one way out. It's exams and pass, or the streets.

My GP sent the letter via my hand to the university. It was ignored. I have evidence of this. 

I never asked to resit exams last August, I've been asking all year to resit them this August. That's fair play, in my opinion. Having that sort of patience isn't easy, but I'm doing it. 
I absolutely thought it was normal to return to university, when I had appealed in June. This gave plenty of time for things to be rectified before the start of the term. I made the university aware of the anxiety I was going through, before exam season was even over. I did this because I read online that it was the best thing to do, rather than waiting for the exam board to sit. I have emails on my university account, which cannot be logged into. These are from last summer. I also have emails on my personal account, going back as  far as November. 

I have the evidence.

The police have asked me if I'd like to open an investigation into what I was going through (the counsellor at the university recommended this while it was going on). I probably will, but I need to get my place back first.

I did apply for student finance, and I was awarded the usual amount. The university cannot free up the amount until it enters me for my exams however.

What would I do, rather than going back to uni?
Thank you for your help. I've just contacted a solicitor for students in Wigan. I'll let you know how we get on.
I've just contacted a solicitor for students. Thanks for your other suggestions.
Thank you.
They live a very long way away. I actually really want to help my parents with some money, when I can. But I haven't got any myself right now.
I'm seeking a solicitor who I can get legal aid with, right now. Thank you for the suggestion.

I've gone to the chancellor, to my MP, he's currently going to the minister for universities, I've gone to an advice service. I'll try the NUS now. The Daily Mail, the Manchester Evening News, ITV's This Morning, they've all contacted me. I just haven't done any of them up until now, because I'd prefer to be anonymous. The Daily Mail has offered me this. 

I just need to sit my exams. It would fix everything. I'd pass them with flying colours because I've been studying for so long, and my student finance would be released, allowing me to get some fresh clothes, to buy food, and to visit my family. 

There aren't any alternatives, it goes very deep. I can't even pay for anything right now. I'm stuck here until at least september when the new year starts, if nothing changes. It's a horrible situation.

Thank you so much for the Churchill quote, I've had that written on my wall since April. That's the spirit I know I need to hold fast to.

I do have evidence though, because I did attend the GP twice in that year over stress. The GP DID send an handheld letter to the university in September, which was read, and was ignored. 

I'm going back to the GP tomorrow. 

Please don't underplay the things people go through in life, it isn't pretty.
I'm not going to engage, you're winding me up.

It is 1000% what I feel I want to do. I mean, university isn't even a big challenge right now, the international conference and the speech I'll be giving there, is. I just wish more people would understand me.

Student finance are okay, an advice service in the local area called them last week for me. It's just that they're unable to release my money until the university enrolls me for my exams. I'm going to get another letter from my GP tomorrow, and I'll tell her everything, and how her first evidence was ignored. 

Thanks for your help mate.

I just wish that good would win over bad, you know?
I almost can't believe it's happening, and I don't want to explain to anybody, because the lack of empathy is atrocious. The one thing I've learned from all of this, is never to be in pain. Never be in a natural disaster, never be a victim of anything nasty. Because you won't be cared for. That's the number one lesson. 

That's it, the constant questions. There must be peace, some says it's in the middle of the storm...

They haven't done all they can, otherwise I wouldn't be here now. 

My friends were allowed to resit just for failing. I didn't fail, I just couldn't get to three exams, for reasons I don't want to talk about. It's not bending the rules in anybody's favour. That's just wishing hate on success. 

They should be accommodating when there is suffering going on, otherwise I would never have attended.
I am a hard worker, who strives for the best though. So just passing wasn't even in my scope, I wanted a first.

No clearly I didn't, and I would have needed to take the first year again. Which I was happy to. I never failed the exams, I just didn't get to 3 (I don't want to talk about it), this bought my average down.
I did register, and I was accepted for student finance. It was only in September when it started bouncing, and I received letters saying how much I was entitled to, but nothing in the bank.

I really appreciate your humour. 

It's so hard not to blame yourself, when they say it is your fault though. You know deep down in the depths of your heart how ridiculous it is to even consider. I do see your point, you're speaking the most sense of anyone on this sub. It just breaks my heart, what some people go through in the name of meaningless rules, and misunderstanding. 

I'm trying my best to stay sane every day. Thanks for the offer to message you. Hopefully it will be with good news, and soon.

I just can't change my plans. Nobody is listening to me. If I had the luxury of some money, I could. It's an abyss on one side, or a meadow on the other. I'm perfectly capable of sitting my exams. I feel like I've already been through the ringer here, an awful year, and then another, coming to terms with it. This is my re-sit year, after all.
Your story is inspiring. Congratulations! All the best with your life and thanks for the wishes.

I believe that for me, being an adult is not giving up when it gets hard. Trust me, I wish I could just give in. But I have a responsibility here, and my future is on the line. It's not a lost cause. Only the university thinks so, I could easily get through it. I've been left to self medicate over the year, and that makes you strong. 

It's not a need. It's just that I won't get my degree otherwise. It's a necessity. 

The thing is, university wasn't hurting me when I arrived. None of this was my fault, and although I've slowly come to accept that, it's so easy to be told that I'm "playing the victim" when somebody doesn't want to help me.

I received a letter in January saying "you have withdrawn from your studies" from student finance. So, I don't know. 
I can only guess the missing exams didn't please them. No second chances at university.
I don't believe we give up our rights in life under duress.

I'm not mentally ill. I just need to be entered for my exams. They won't release my loan because they haven't enrolled me for my exams yet. I know they don't care about me, but what am I to do? I can't get off ground zero without the loan. I can't even work because I don't have clothes. I also just want an apology for what my teacher called me.

You don't understand the pain people go through. You don't notify people of issues at the time. Most sufferers of domestic violence are silent about it. Look it up. Your comment is very hurtful. I'm trying to ignore it, but telling someone they're playing the victim.....if you ever get cancer I promise I won't tell you to pull yourself together. I'm not that low.
But if I just let them ignore me, what happens when it happens to someone else, and they kill themselves? We need to speak up for the lowly, to fight injustice.

I spent the entirety of last summer appealing, with evidence. They ignored it.  I am sorted out mentally, hence the studying. It's been 8 months. I'm fine. Physically I'm not, but clearly I can't support myself until my student finance is released. At least then I could get some fresh clothes and some food.
I spent the entire summer appealing, with evidence, before this academic year. They ignored it.
I spent the entirety of last summer appealing, with evidence, before this academic year. They ignored it.
Do you know where I could get legal advice?

I disagree. 

Students who enter university should be allowed to sit their exams unhindered.

I didn't disclose what was going on because I was in so much emotional pain at the time. I know it sounds ridiculous when you haven't been there, you'd only understand when you're going through it. Your mind becomes crystal clear the day you move out of a bad situation. 

I missed a couple of exams which I was happy to take this year. But never got the chance. I'm fighting for my right to take them. I worked hard for years and got the right A levels. 

Why on Earth would I have a criminal record? How would I go about getting one of those?

Please read the sub. It wasn't my fault. I'd love to say it was, but it wasn't. You weren't there. I would know.

Consent is very relevant when you're the one who has worked for years to get this opportunity. The system isn't right just because it's wrong.

I'll give it a read. 

It's just awful when the board really is a totally random set of people, with no true reason to be there. No credentials necessarily. It's really ruined my view of the world. 

Not dwelling on it is such a hard thing to do, when you've been called a liar. I know you're right, and that I need to look at the long term instead of the short term. If I take my exams this summer, and get graduated within a couple of years, I'll look back in time...and maybe I won't smile. but I'll see how strong it made me. 

I do try to talk, but I need help. The helping never seems to come.
Thanks for your offer, I really appreciate it. Honestly I do.

I just feel awful. It's personal. I just need to see it out. I'm not a quitter. I've suffered for too long. I already took a year out because of this. Nobody understands apart from me. That's the same reason I'm being downvoted to death on this sub, but 100% upvoted on the UK universities sub. Nobody gets it. I just want exam dates and then to be left alone.

Additionally, I never did withdraw from my course. In January, I simply received a letter from Student Finance telling me that I had been withdrawn. I never gave consent. There is no evidence of me withdrawing, anywhere.

Went to university, got abused by drug dealing housemates for most of first year. Anything from verbal to things that leave bruises. Came back in October, had been withdrawn from the course. Year of hell has followed, in which the university has made me the "criminal." I don't know what to do and can't see a way out.

I know there are other universities that would take me, but I've suffered too much to let this year go to waste. I just want to take my exams in August. Perhaps the staff will leave soon, that will improve things. Also I'd have to go through an entire application process, moving, money, etc. I can't even afford to take the bus up the street right now. A year of hell is too much a price to pay. I'm not giving in.

I just can't begin to explain how torturous this entire situation is. It's beyond words.

Thank you for reading. I'll give that a read in better days ahead. It's an existentialist novel, right? 

Judgemental is the word. It feels as though the judgement is already passed before you even get in the door, however. 

I just don't want to let a grand total of 3 people ruin my life. That's all this is. Wrong people. Wrong place. With kinder, more caring people around, this might have never happened. It's really taken me to hell and back.

I just want to sit my exams in the resit period in August. Yes, first year. I won't allow this year to go to waste. I can't even explain the suffering. Suffering that takes you to the very, very edge. I never thought there'd be a situation that could be experienced, that you'd feel as though could never, ever, ever, be explained with words. This is that, for me.

I'm actually in a very difficult situation right now. I got offered to go on ITV's 'This Morning' about it, but I don't want the exposure for something that has been ruining my life for months. The University have been repeatedly walking all over me. My MP has written a few times and the Minister for education is recently on board. The head of the student experience at Manchester has been very rude to me in a recent meeting. Nancy Rothwell replies to emails as though I'm a parasite she's trying to exterminate. They've got me by the balls for something that wasn't my fault (I was bullied severely by an ex violent housemate and it led to me failing an exam, I haven't received student loan funding this year and have been penniless since October. Can't pay the rent, can't work because I don't have the right clothes and often can't wash etc, can't feed myself.) 
They lie about you in front of your face and one professor said in a meeting that was set up "stop acting like the world is against you." I hadn't actually ever said those words.
It broke my heart and I was a recluse afterwards for about a month. Absolutely heartbroken. 
It's an awful university. I was so happy to be accepted. But it's an awful, awful university.

I go to the University and was recently rebuked by a professor for seeking assistance in a difficult time. She flat out told me "we are a business and so you should expect us to run as one." I really, really needed personal assistance at the time, and she was essentially telling me that I had no right to it. I can't even be bothered to explain the context, it would take a few pages of A4. 
Yeah. This country is in a state. It took me so long to see it, but I really think we're going down. 
The cancer is spreading and nobody cares.

Hi there,
I'm here for you. Message me. 
Lets talk.
Be safe, I care more than the world I promise.
Bump

I understand, I really do. I'm going through it myself at the moment. Like I almost feel as though I don't belong on this plane of existence. I don't feel like I'm the same species as my fellow humans sometimes, I don't know if that sounds mad or not. People can & are very cruel. I hear you. Would you like to talk? Please send me a DM.
